exercise.name: Plate Front Raise
steps: Stand tall holding a weight plate by its sides, arms down.
Raise the plate straight out in front up to eye level.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing, a weight plate held by its sides between flat palms, arms down. Straight arms raise the plate in front up to eye level, then lower. Front delts are the target; upper chest helps.

setup.target: Plate held by its sides between flat palms.

movement.path: Straight arms rise in front (library step 2).

muscles.emg: Frontal raise: anterior deltoid greater than every lateral raise (S1).
Frontal raise: pectoralis major greater than every lateral raise (S1).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Hips forward, trunk tipped back to throw the plate up.

sources.citation: Coratella G, Tornatore G, Longo S, Esposito F, Ce E. 2020. An electromyographic analysis of lateral raise variations and frontal raise in competitive bodybuilders. Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(17):6015. doi:10.3390/ijerph17176015
sources.what_it_gave: Frontal raise: anterior deltoid and pectoralis major show greater EMG than in every lateral raise variation.

sources.citation: Campos YAC, Vianna JM, Guimaraes MP, et al. 2020. Different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals. J Hum Kinet 75:5-14. doi:10.2478/hukin-2020-0033
sources.what_it_gave: Anterior deltoid ~21-33% MVIC across presses and raises at 60% 1RM; shoulder-flexion work loads the front delt most.
The steps the app shows; the pictures must match them.

clip_check.check: Both palms on the plate rim
Front delts strongest red, chest lighter
